That CC example makes the case really well. Premium-as-noise-filter is the right call -- and it's actually elegant because premium is already the dominant scoring axis (0-6 of 10 points). So the V/OI bonus wouldn't be fighting the existing logic, it'd be amplifying contracts that already score well on premium but happen to land in thin OI names where the positioning signal is clearest.

Implementation-wise, your two tiers map cleanly into `_calculate_flow_score()` as a third additive component. I'm thinking something like 0-2 points for V/OI, gated on those premium floors. A $2M premium contract with 99x V/OI would already score ~5-6 on premium alone -- adding 1.5-2 points for the V/OI signal bumps it firmly into high-conviction territory, which feels right for CC-level activity.

The strike clustering idea is valuable but architecturally different. Right now every contract is scored independently inside `_calculate_unified_score()` -- it has no awareness of what other alerts fired in the same cycle. To detect matched-volume spreads, we'd need a post-scoring correlation pass that looks at recent alerts for the same symbol and expiry. Totally doable, but it's a separate feature, not something I'd stuff into the V/OI bonus.

Ben, want us to spec this out as a concrete implementation? The V/OI bonus itself is small -- maybe 30 lines in `_calculate_flow_score()` plus the OI field plumbed through from the contract data. The strike clustering would be a second phase.
